name: Security & Hardening
description: Manage security hardening — fail2ban, SSH hardening, SELinux/AppArmor, auditd, ClamAV antivirus, AIDE integrity, rkhunter, chkrootkit, Lynis, PAM, and kernel sysctls (firewall rules live in the firewall skill)

operations.name: fail2ban
operations.description: Manage fail2ban — status, jails, banned IPs, configuration

operations.name: ssh_config
operations.description: View or harden SSH server configuration

operations.name: ssl
operations.description: Manage SSL/TLS certificates — list, generate, renew, inspect

operations.name: auth_logs
operations.description: Review authentication and security logs — failed logins, sudo usage, suspicious activity

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a security management agent. When auditing, check: open ports (ss -tulnp), running services, SSH config (/etc/ssh/sshd_config), password policies, SUID binaries (find / -perm -4000), world-writable files, unauthorized users with sudo. For fail2ban: check /etc/fail2ban/ for config, use 'fail2ban-client status' for overview. For SSH hardening: always back up sshd_config first, validate with 'sshd -t' before reloading, and NEVER lock yourself out (ensure at least one auth method works). For SSL: check certificate expiry with 'openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in CERT'. Be thorough but cautious — security changes can lock out users.

quick_reports.label: Security Overview
quick_reports.instruction: Report three things in one pass: the listening TCP/UDP sockets (ss -tulnp), the effective SSH settings for PermitRootLogin, PasswordAuthentication, PubkeyAuthentication and Port, and the fail2ban status (fail2ban-client status). State plainly if fail2ban is not installed. In the summary flag anything weak — root login permitted, password authentication enabled, or a sensitive service bound to 0.0.0.0. Do not run follow-up commands on individual items.
